subject: Accounting
title: The Audit Opinion
description: A quick win: understand The Audit Opinion.

hook.text: Before trusting any financial statement, flip to the auditor's letter. It tells you everything.

buildup.text: An independent auditor reviews the statements and issues an opinion on their accuracy.

discovery.text: A 'clean' or unqualified opinion means the auditor found no major problems.

twist.text: A 'qualified' opinion means issues were found. A 'disclaimer' means the auditor couldn't verify.

climax.text: Going concern warnings in the audit letter have predicted company collapses many times.

punchline.text: The auditor's opinion is the trust rating of the numbers.

quiz.question: What does an unqualified audit opinion mean?
options: The company is unqualified for listing
The auditor couldn't complete the review

details.summary: The audit opinion is the external auditor's formal statement about whether financial statements are fairly presented. This topic explains the four types of opinions—unqualified, qualified, adverse, and disclaimer—and what each means for investors.
details.whyItMatters: The audit opinion is the first thing sophisticated investors check. A clean opinion doesn't guarantee accuracy, but anything other than clean is a serious warning signal.
takeaways: An unqualified (clean) opinion means the auditor found no material misstatements in the financial statements
A qualified opinion indicates specific issues or scope limitations that don't permeate the entire statements
A going concern paragraph warns that the company may not survive another year—the most serious red flag

faq.question: What are the four types of audit opinions?
faq.answer: Unqualified (clean): statements are fairly presented. Qualified: statements are fair except for specific issues. Adverse: statements are materially misstated and not reliable. Disclaimer: the auditor couldn't gather sufficient evidence to form an opinion.

faq.question: What is a going concern opinion?
faq.answer: A going concern paragraph in the audit report means the auditor has substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue operating for another 12 months. It's the most serious warning an auditor can issue and often precedes bankruptcy or financial restructuring.
